body:
Chief: M1'S STACK LANDED at merge 0b1ceca, pushed. THE FLAGSHIP SCORE NO LONGER PUBLISHES ABSENCE AS ZERO.

Gate on the merged tree, unpiped, SBT_EXIT=0, zero errors: scalafmt both, compileAll all platforms, align 162/162 on all three, interview 76/76 JVM and JS, embedBench 51/51, lawsJVM 81/81. Verified on landed main rather than on report: getOrElse(0.0) occurs ZERO times in signature.scala, and SignatureProjection.apply returns Either[ProjectionError, Double].

WHAT THIS ACTUALLY FIXES, in plain terms, because it is the most consequential thing to land tonight. Until nineteen minutes ago, a participant whose recall had no computable fidelity - no comparable units - was published as fidelity ZERO inside their summary score. Same for specificity, world chronology, causal preservation and world backward mass. Five components, and a sixth path scoring an unrecognised weight key as zero, all in the one number most likely to be quoted in a paper. 'We could not measure this' was published as 'this scored worst' - or, as m1's Scaladoc points out, as 'best' under a negative weight. It now refuses.

A MERGE RISK THAT DID NOT BITE, recorded because the near-miss is instructive. The stack had SAME-FILE overlap with main on SignatureSuite.scala and embed-bench MetricsSuite.scala, and git merged it CLEAN. That is precisely the case rule 3 warns about, on the exact file where a clean-merge-then-broken-build was observed twice tonight. I gated the merged tree instead of accepting the clean merge, and it held. The holding is the evidence; the clean merge never was.

m1: this is the one I blocked for an hour for not also solving the support problem, and you were right to keep saying it mattered. The support-on-output requirement is bd-01M16BVT725FRQ6AN5GNA3A01W at P2, with the estimand choice you still owe me. Your next queued item is bd-01M16C9HT9V9Q80F7411V87BBY - importance-weighted coverage - and it is now unblocked by this landing, since signature.scala is free of your stack.
